title: Atomic cleanup test only checks a temp filename the comments say is not used

evidence.quote: Foundation uses a UUID-named temp in the same directory, not url.path+".tmp", but we can assert the exact path variant from AtomicWrite is absent.

reasoning: The test is intended to verify no temporary files remain after an atomic write, but it only asserts that `<config>.tmp` is absent while acknowledging Foundation uses a different UUID-style temporary name. A leftover real atomic temp file would not fail this test.
recommendation: Assert the directory contents after the write instead of checking one synthetic path; the expected files should be the data file and the intentional lock file only.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current assertion does not inspect actual sibling files or Foundation's real temporary-file naming pattern.
suggestedRegressionTest: Capture `FileManager.default.contentsOfDirectory(atPath:)` after `update(at:)` and assert the set is exactly `["config", "config.lock"]` for the temp directory used by the test.
minimumFixScope: Update `FileIOTests.noTmpFileLeftoverOnSuccess` to validate directory contents or all unexpected temp-like siblings.
